messages.subject: low discrepancy sequences
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm currently making a R package (named randtoolbox and under GNU GPL)  
with pseudo and quasi random generators. And I wanted to add Sobol and  
Halton low discrepancy sequences to my package.

But I found out the package fOptions already implemented that stuff.  
So I ask you the permission to use your Fortran code (i.e. 085A- 
LowDiscrepancy.f) in my package.

I already use foreign codes under GNU GPL: the C code from Matsumoto  
and Saito for SF-mersenne twister.

If you accept, there will be an explicit banner in my help page saying  
I use the Rmetrics code such as for SF-mersenne twister.

Otherwise could you advise me some code on www.mcqmc.org/Software.html?

Thanks in advance

Best regards

Christophe Dutang

PS : my package randtoolbox can be found on CRAN.
	[[alternative HTML version deleted]]

messages.subject: CashOrNothingOption
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rmetrics core

In the "d" term in the CashOrNothingOption-Function in the R-package fExoticOptions it is somewhat confusing to use b (instead of r?).
In my opinion it should be like

d = (log(S/X) + (r + b - sigma^2/2) * Time)/(sigma * sqrt(Time)), 

resulting in the standard formula if there is no cost-of-carry. Do I mix things up?

Best regards, David

messages.subject: bug in as.data.frame.timeDate with 'anonymous' object
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

I think I have stumbled upon a bug in as.data.frame.timeDate in the
fCalendar package. From the unit tests for that package, 

> TC=timeCalendar(2006)
> as.data.frame(TC)
       GMT:TC
1  2006-01-01
2  2006-02-01
3  2006-03-01
4  2006-04-01
5  2006-05-01
6  2006-06-01
7  2006-07-01
8  2006-08-01
9  2006-09-01
10 2006-10-01
11 2006-11-01
12 2006-12-01

which works as expected. But compare this to a call without creating an
intermediate variable:

> as.data.frame(timeCalendar(2006))
Error in names(x) <- value : 
  'names' attribute [2] must be the same length as the vector [1]
> traceback()
4: `colnames<-.default`(`*tmp*`, value = c("GMT:timeCalendar", "GMT:2006"
   ))
3: `colnames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = c("GMT:timeCalendar", "GMT:2006"
   ))
2: as.data.frame.timeDate(timeCalendar(2006))
1: as.data.frame(timeCalendar(2006))


The problem seems to arise from as.data.frame.timeDate's attempt to
construct sensible column names:

> as.data.frame.timeDate
function (x, ...) 
{
    myTZ = Sys.getenv("TZ")
    Sys.setenv(TZ = "GMT")
    stopifnot(inherits(x, "timeDate"))
    ans = as.data.frame.POSIXlt(x at Data, ...)
    colnames(ans) = paste(x at FinCenter, ":", substitute(x), sep = "")
    attr(ans, "control") = c(FinCenter = x at FinCenter)
    Sys.setenv(TZ = myTZ)
    ans
}

Perhaps there could be some default name when substitute(x) returns a vector
of length > 1?


I am using R 2.7.0 on Windows XP SP2. I have fCalendar version 270.75. Let
me know if you need further information. I did not see any posts on this
issue on the R-SIG-Finance list, which is a bit surprising. I a convert from
S-Plus, though, so perhaps I am not looking in the right place.

Chris Green

x<-read.table("C:/Documents and

hillPlot.summary(x, plottype="alpha")

shaparmHill(x, p = 0.05, xiRange = NULL,doplot = TRUE, plottype =
c("both")

 

In the end I am hoping to get an optimal parameter to fit the
distribution.
